chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh ibn Nusayr, from al-Ubaydi, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Ismail ibn Jabir who said:

I was with Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in the vicinity of Makka, when he said to me: O Ismail, proceed until you reach Marra or Usfan, and ask if any incident has occurred in Madina. He said: I went out until I reached Marra but did not encounter anyone. Then I proceeded until I reached Usfan but did not encounter anyone. I set out from Usfan, and when I left it, a caravan carrying olives from Usfan met me. I said to them: Is there any incident which has occurred in Madina? They said: No, except the killing of this Iraqi called al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays. He said: I returned to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so when he saw me he said to me: O Ismail, al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays has been killed? I said: Yes. He said: By Allah, he has entered paradise.

key_terms.الْمَعْلَى بْنُ خُنَيْسٍ: al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.عَسْفَانَ: Usfan, a station on the road between Makka and Madina

ai.seo_question: Who was al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays and what did Imam al-Sadiq say about his death?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kashi’s *Rijal* highlights the intimate bond between Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and his companion Ismail ibn Jabir during the critical period following the death of Imam al-Baqir (AS). The Imam’s immediate confirmation of al-Mu'alla ibn Khunays’ entry into Paradise underscores the Shia doctrine of *'ismah* (infallibility) and the Imam’s divine knowledge (*'ilm al-ladunni*) regarding the fate of his loyal followers amidst political turmoil.
